candidates.hypothesis: Adding the derived 'hourmin_bucket' categorical feature alongside existing fields will improve user preference ranking by capturing time-of-day periodicity.
candidates.information_value: Determines whether granular temporal features provide signal beyond static user-item interactions.
candidates.mechanism: User viewing behavior changes by time of day (morning vs. late night). Encoding hourmin_bucket into the feature vector allows the FM to learn time-dependent user biases.

candidates.hypothesis: Replacing pointwise logloss with a pairwise BPR (Bayesian Personalized Ranking) loss on user impression pairs will better align with the ranking metric (GAUC and nDCG).
candidates.information_value: Establishes whether ranking-aligned losses outperform simple pointwise cross-entropy for KuaiRand impressions.
candidates.mechanism: Pointwise logloss trains the model on absolute probability calibration rather than relative item ordering. BPR directly optimizes the relative score difference between clicked and unclicked items for each user.

candidates.hypothesis: Implementing a negative-to-positive ratio downsampling or hard negative mining strategy during training will accelerate convergence and reduce overfitting.
candidates.information_value: Reveals whether training sample distribution tuning helps mitigate the growing train-dev gap.
candidates.mechanism: KuaiRand has many more unclicked impressions than clicks. Balancing the training batch or emphasizing borderline negatives prevents the bias toward non-clicks and sharpens user ranking.

candidates.hypothesis: Increasing L2 regularization on the embedding table (V and W) from 1e-6 to 1e-4 will suppress the growing train-dev gap without harming validation performance.
candidates.information_value: Measures the sensitivity of the second-order FM to embedding norm penalties.
candidates.mechanism: The current champion shows a widening train-dev gap (train primary 0.687 vs dev primary 0.602), indicating overfitting. Stronger L2 regularization penalizes large feature weights and improves generalization.

candidates.hypothesis: Adding a global bias interaction or scaling factor to second-order factorization machine terms will enhance feature cross expressivity.
candidates.information_value: Tests whether minor structural adjustments to the FM bilinear interaction can improve ranking accuracy.
candidates.mechanism: A modified interaction layer that weighs second-order feature combinations differently can capture stronger non-linear relationships than standard FM without increasing parameter count significantly.

candidates.hypothesis: Applying temperature scaling or rank-sigmoid calibration on model predictions prior to evaluation will stabilize scoring distributions.
candidates.information_value: Determines if post-hoc score calibration affects ranking metrics like GAUC and nDCG.
candidates.mechanism: Scaling logits with a learned temperature parameter can soften overconfident predictions, improving ranking robustness.

architecture_verdicts.reason: Modifying the second-order Factorization Machine architecture carries too high an implementation risk and potential for regression given the strictly limited 1-evaluation remaining budget.

judge.convergence_note: With 1 evaluation remaining before the convergence check, selecting a low-risk config optimization (OR1) is the safest way to curb overfitting and secure a positive gain.

ranking.note: Directly tackles the observable overfitting (train-dev gap growing to 0.085) with a simple config-only L2 regularization adjustment. High probability of stabilizing or improving generalization within the 1-iteration budget.
Adds time-of-day feature periodicity. Solid idea, but requires code changes and may require tuning vocabulary sizes.
Downsampling negative impressions helps address label imbalance, but requires modifying training batch sampling loops.
BPR pairwise loss better aligns with ranking, but requires writing a new step method and gradient formulas from scratch.
Structural FM interaction tweaks. High risk for the remaining single evaluation budget.
Post-hoc score calibration generally preserves ranking order (GAUC/nDCG) and rarely improves ranking metrics.

judge.why_selected: With exactly 1 evaluation remaining in our live budget, we must prioritize maximum reliability and a high probability of success. The current champion exhibits a clear sign of overfitting: the train primary score climbs rapidly to 0.686 while dev primary plateaus around 0.601, yielding an expanding train-dev gap of ~0.085. Candidate OR1 directly addresses this via L2 regularization on the embedding tables with zero architectural or code risk (config-only edit), making it the optimal exploit move.

reflection.prediction_comment: The negative delta (-0.0009) indicates the penalty was slightly too harsh, though it successfully narrowed the train-dev gap.
reflection.remaining_uncertainty: Whether milder regularization can capture a net gain.
reflection.what_happened: Increasing L2 regularization on the embedding tables from 1e-6 to 1e-4 lowered the train-dev gap (dropping train primary from 0.687 to 0.634), but slightly hurt validation primary performance (0.6008 vs. champion 0.6017).
reflection.why: The hypothesis correctly identified overfitting (a large train-dev gap), but increasing L2 regularization too aggressively over-penalized the embedding weights, reducing model capacity on validation data slightly more than the gain from reduced variance.
